evals.prompt: The project in evals/files/shared-gif-project changed a user-visible browser settings flow. Its build, start, browser-control and ignored evidence paths are declared. Record the requested GIF evidence from the real build and report what was verified.
evals.expected_output: The run records one isolated real-build interaction, keeps all frames from that run, encodes and inspects the GIF, reports the application origin and real-versus-substituted services, and leaves the media outside tracked content.
assertions: The evidence comes from one isolated run of the declared real build.
The application origin, state isolation and real-versus-substituted services are reported.
The encoded GIF is inspected after encoding and its metadata is reported.
No media is committed to a tracked branch.

evals.prompt: The provided project changed a user-visible browser UI, but the host has no browser-control capability, no declared Playwright fallback, and no ffmpeg or ffprobe. Finish the evidence task now.
evals.expected_output: The run preserves any possible preparation, does not claim that the UI was demonstrated, and hands off the missing capture, runtime and media capabilities with the unfinished GIF evidence and a resumable next step.
assertions: The run names the missing browser and media capabilities.
It does not substitute source inspection for the required rendered evidence.
It reports the unfinished evidence and a resumable next step.

evals.prompt: The user explicitly requests a fixture-only GIF because the real external provider is unavailable. The app in evals/files/shared-gif-project is the fixture, and evals/files/fixture-origin.md records that authorization. Record and verify that fixture demonstration without claiming it proves the real provider flow.
evals.expected_output: The run records and verifies one fixture demonstration and clearly labels the fixture, unavailable real provider and the evidence boundary.
assertions: The explicit fixture request authorizes the substitute recording.
The run labels the evidence as fixture-based rather than real-provider evidence.
The encoded GIF is still captured from one isolated run and inspected after encoding.
The report states which real behavior the evidence does not prove.
